items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Corollary 8.8.5 at source lines 2464-2471: for n >= 0 a map f : A -> B is n-connected if and only if trunc 0 f is an isomorphism, pi_k(f) is an isomorphism for k <= n and pi_{n+1}(f) is surjective. The converse direction, which is the substance of the proof (source lines 2472-2483), is not formal: one first has to feed the group-theoretic hypotheses into the long exact sequence of the fibration to learn that the fiber has vanishing homotopy groups up to n and contractible 0-truncation (lines 2474-2476), then convert that into contractibility of trunc n of the fiber over points of the form f(a) by the Whitehead criterion (line 2477), and finally extend to an arbitrary b : B by a two-step argument in which surjectivity of trunc 0 f provides a preimage in the truncation and the fact that contractibility is a mere proposition allows the truncations to be stripped twice (lines 2479-2482).
